German Chocolate Loaf Cake with Sticky Coconut Pecan Topping

A dark chocolate loaf cake with a no-cook date caramel, coconut and toasted pecan topping, all the flavor of German chocolate cake without the layers or the cooked frosting.

By Pamela

Sep 15, 2026

This German chocolate cake recipe is a loaf cake, not a layer cake: one deeply chocolatey loaf (with a little espresso powder to make the chocolate taste more like itself) under a sticky, caramel-like topping of Medjool dates, shredded coconut, and toasted pecans.

There is no cooked custard frosting and no stacking! It’s easily made dairy-free with plant butter and oat or soy milk, and it comes together in one 9 x 5 loaf pan (did I mention it’s easy?!).

Why You’ll Love This German Chocolate Cake Recipe

I think we all know this about the classic version: it is a project. Three layers, a frosting you stand at the stove and stir until it decides to thicken (and it takes its time), and then everything has to cool completely before you can assemble it. I have made the real deal, and my grain-free German chocolate cake from the Sweet Laurel cookbook is worth every minute for a birthday. But for a random Tuesday in September? No way!

So I took a classic, moist chocolate loaf and gave it a modern (and dare I say irresistible) twist. The topping is a gooey, caramel-like mixture of dates, coconut, and pecans that you make in the blender. No egg yolks to temper, no evaporated milk, no stovetop, and no chance of it not setting up because there is nothing to set. It has all the German chocolate cake vibes with a fraction of the work.

Ingredient Notes

Here are some tips on key ingredients. You’ll find the rest (plus measurements) in the recipe card below.

For the Chocolate Loaf

  • Unsweetened cocoa powder: Dutch-process or natural cocoa powder work here, and this is one of the rare recipes where I mean that. The loaf rises with baking powder only (no baking soda), so the acidity of the cocoa doesn’t affect the rise the way it does in a lot of chocolate cakes. Dutch-process gives you a darker, more mellow loaf, and natural gives you a slightly lighter, brighter one. Both delicious!
  • Espresso powder: Optional, but I wouldn’t skip it. Two teaspoons don’t make the cake taste like coffee, they make the chocolate taste MORE like chocolate. Instant coffee works too.
  • Unsalted butter or plant butter: Room temperature, and I mean actually soft. Cold butter won’t cream with the sugar which means you’ll have lumps that never go away. Plant butter makes this loaf dairy-free.

For the Date Caramel and Topping

  • Medjool dates: Medjools are the soft, sticky, caramel-y ones, and they blend into a sauce that genuinely tastes like caramel without any cream or refined sugar. This is the same trick behind my sticky toffee pudding cake made with Medjool dates. Six pitted dates, about 3/4 cup packed, soaked in hot water for 30 minutes so they blend completely smooth. Deglet Noor dates are drier and firmer, and I have not tested them here.
  • Brown rice syrup and maple syrup: The maple is for flavor, the brown rice syrup is for that sticky, chewy pull that makes this taste like the classic frosting. I have not tested this with all maple syrup. My guess is it would be looser and sweeter.

Recipe Variations

  • Filled loaf: Once the cake is completely cool, slice it in half lengthwise and slather half of the date-coconut topping in the middle, then put the top back on and spread the rest over the top. It looks like a layer cake and eats like one, and it took you an extra two minutes.
  • Smaller loaf pan: You can use an 8 1/2 x 4 1/2 pan, but it will take slightly longer to bake and the top will be more domed. Start checking at 65 minutes.
  • Gluten-free: I have not made this loaf with gluten-free flour, so I can’t promise anything. If you need a gluten-free chocolate cake I have tested, my grain-free options in the recipes below are the safer bet.

If you like the idea of a loaf sweetened with dates instead of sugar, my banana bread sweetened only with dates is a different cake entirely, but it’s the one to make.

How to Make German Chocolate Cake Recipe (Loaf Version)

Step 1: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Lightly grease a 9 x 5 loaf pan and line it with parchment paper, leaving a little overhang on the long sides so you can lift the cake out later. Put the dates in a bowl with 1 cup of hot water now so they soak while you make the batter.

Step 2: In a medium mixing bowl, beat together the butter, sugar, salt, vanilla, baking powder, espresso powder and cocoa. The mixture will be somewhat clumpy and that is correct, so don’t keep beating trying to make it smooth.

Step 3: Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each one, then scrape down the sides and bottom of the bowl. This is where the batter turns glossy and smooth. 

Step 4: Stir in half the flour. Add all of the milk, beating on low speed to combine. Add the remaining flour on low speed until JUST combined. Overbeating once the flour is in makes a tough loaf, and nobody wants a tough loaf.

Step 5: Pour the batter into the prepared pan and bake for 60 to 70 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. (I know that’s a big window. Loaf cakes are thick, ovens vary, and a 9 x 5 pan and an 8 1/2 x 4 1/2 pan bake differently. Trust the toothpick.)

Step 6: Remove the cake from the oven and let it cool in the pan for 10 minutes. Then lift it out and let it cool completely on a wire rack. Completely. If you top a warm cake, the coconut oil in the topping melts and the whole thing slides off the sides.

Step 7: Make the topping. Drain the dates, reserving the soaking liquid. Put the dates, coconut oil, maple syrup, brown rice syrup, almond butter, vanilla, sea salt and 2 Tablespoons of the date-soaking liquid in a blender or food processor and process until completely smooth. Keep the rest of the date liquid nearby, just in case.

Step 8: Pour the date sauce into a medium bowl and stir in the coconut and pecans. If it’s too stiff to spread, add a little more of the reserved date liquid, a spoonful at a time, until it’s spreadable but still thick. Spread it over the cooled cake and slice thick.

Recipe Tips

  • Butter, eggs, and milk should all be room temperature. This is the one thing every good German chocolate cake recipe agrees on, and for good reason: cold ingredients don’t emulsify, and a broken batter bakes into a dense, greasy loaf.
  • When you beat the butter, sugar and cocoa together in Step 2, it will look like wet sand, not like frosting. It comes together once the eggs go in.
  • A 9 x 5 chocolate loaf is heavy, and flipping it out of the pan upside down can crack it. Lift it out by the parchment instead.
  • Cool the cake all the way before topping. I said it above and I’ll say it again. Warm cake, melting topping, sad sliding mess. I know it’s hard, but wait for it to cool completely.
  • Loosen the topping with date water, not plain water. It’s already sweet and a little caramel-y, so it thins the sauce without watering down the flavor. Add it a spoonful at a time so you don’t thin it out too much.
  • Toast the pecans while the oven is preheating. They need a few minutes in the oven anyway and you’re already standing there.

How to Serve German Chocolate Loaf Cake

Thick slices, with coffee, ideally in the afternoon. This is not a dainty cake and it shouldn’t be sliced like one. If you’re serving it for dessert, a little unsweetened whipped cream (or whipped coconut cream to keep it dairy-free) is nice against the sticky topping, but honestly it doesn’t need anything.

Storage & Make Ahead

  • Store your topped cake at room temperature for 2 to 3 days on the counter. It’s moist and holds up well stored this way. You can store it in the fridge for up to 5 days. Keep in mind that the topping will firm up because the coconut oil solidifies when it’s cold, so let slices sit out for 15 to 20 minutes before serving.
  • Freeze the loaf untopped. Wrap it well in foil, then in a freezer bag, up to 3 months, and defrost overnight on the counter before making the topping fresh. I don’t recommend freezing the finished, topped cake. The texture gets funny once defrosted.
  • Make ahead: The date sauce (before you stir in the coconut and pecans) can be made a day or two ahead and kept in the fridge. Let it come to room temperature and loosen it with a little water if needed before stirring in the coconut and pecans.

Recipe FAQs

What is the key ingredient in German chocolate cake?

Historically, it’s Baker’s German’s Sweet Chocolate, the bar the whole cake was invented to sell. But ask anyone what they remember about a German chocolate cake and they’ll say the coconut and pecans. In this recipe the key ingredient is Medjool dates, which blend into a caramel-like sauce that holds the coconut and pecans together without cooking a custard.

What makes German chocolate cake so moist?

In a classic recipe it’s usually buttermilk or oil in the batter plus a very rich frosting. Here it’s three eggs, whole milk and a full stick of butter in the loaf, and then a sticky topping that seals the top of the cake and keeps it from drying out. The other half of the answer is not overbaking it: pull the loaf as soon as the toothpick comes out clean, not five minutes later.

Is German chocolate cake really from Germany?

No. It’s named after Samuel German, who developed a sweet baking chocolate for Baker’s in 1852. The cake itself is a Texas recipe from 1957 that spread once the chocolate company started promoting it. So it is about as German as I am, which is to say, not at all (I’m Italian, in case you’re new here).

Can I use this topping on a regular German chocolate cake?

I don’t see why not, and if you have a favorite layer cake recipe and just want to skip the cooked frosting, this topping is a much faster route. You’d likely want to double it for a three-layer cake.

German Chocolate Loaf Cake

By Pamela
A dark chocolate loaf cake with a no-cook date caramel, coconut and toasted pecan topping, all the flavor of German chocolate cake without the layers or the cooked frosting.
Servings: 10 10 slices (one 9 x 5 loaf)
Prep Time: 10 minutes mins
Cook Time: 1 hour hr 10 minutes mins
Total Time: 1 hour hr 20 minutes mins
Pin Comment Print

Ingredients 

Cake Ingredients

  • 8 Tablespoons unsalted butter or plant butter, room temperature + extra for greasing the pan
  • 1 ½ cups granulated sugar
  • ¾ teaspoon kosher salt
  • 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
  • ½ teaspoon aluminum-free baking powder
  • Optional: 2 teaspoons espresso powder or instant coffee
  • 2/3 cup unsweetened cocoa, Dutch-process or natural
  • 3 large eggs, at room temperature
  • 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
  • 3/4 cup whole milk, at room temperature or soy milk or oat milk

Date Caramel Sauce

  • 6 Medjool pitted dates, (¾ cup packed), soaked in 1 cup hot water for 30 minutes
  • 3 Tablespoons unrefined coconut oil
  • 3 Tablespoons maple syrup
  • 3 Tablespoons brown rice syrup
  • ¼ cup creamy, raw unsalted almond butter
  • ½ teaspoon vanilla extract
  • ¾ teaspoon sea salt

Topping

  • 1 cup unsweetened shredded coconut, (fine, not big flakes)
  • ⅔ cup toasted pecans
Prevent your screen from going dark

Instructions 

  • Preheat the oven to 350°F. Lightly grease a 9 x 5 loaf pan and line with parchment paper. You can also use an 8 ½ x 4 ½ pan, but it will take slightly long to bake and the top will be more domed.
  • In a medium-sized mixing bowl, beat together the butter, sugar, salt, vanilla, baking powder, espresso powder, cocoa. The mixture will be somewhat clumpy.
  • Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Scrape down the sides and bottom of the bowl.
  • Stir in half the flour.
  • Add all of the milk, beating at low speed to combine.
  • Add the remaining flour at low speed until just combined.
  • Pour the batter into the prepared pan.
  • Bake the cake for 60 to 70 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
  • Remove the cake from the oven and let cool for 10 minutes. Then remove from the pan and allow to cook on a wire rack.
  • Prepare the topping: Combine all sauce ingredients, including 2 Tablespoons of the date-soaking liquid in a blender or food processor and process until completely smooth. Reserve the remaining date liquid just in case you need it.
  • Pour date sauce into a medium bowl and stir in coconut and pecans together. Add additional liquid if needed to loosen it to a spreadable consistency.
  • Spread topping over cooled cake.

Notes

  • Butter, eggs and milk must be at room temperature or the batter can break.
  • The butter-sugar-cocoa mixture looks clumpy before the eggs go in; that is normal.
  • Do not top the cake until it is completely cool or the topping will slide off. 
  • Loosen the topping with the reserved date water, not plain water, a spoonful at a time.
  • Dairy-free: use plant butter and soy or oat milk. The topping is naturally dairy-free.
  • Filled version: slice the cooled loaf in half lengthwise, spread half the topping in the middle, replace the top and spread the rest over the top.
  • Storage: covered at room temperature 2 to 3 days or refrigerated up to 5 days (let slices sit out 15 to 20 minutes so the topping softens). Freeze the untopped loaf, well wrapped, up to 3 months; make the topping fresh after thawing.
